blocks.text: KING OF JUDAH · TWO KINGDOMS
Jehoram. Eight years in Jerusalem, married into Ahab's house.
REIGNEDi
8 years c. 854–841 BC (dates vary)
CAPITAL
Jerusalem
HOUSE
House of David 5th of 20 in Judah
VERDICT
✕ Did evil “and he did evil in the sight of the LORD”
PROPHETS
Elijah
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS REHOBOAM → ZEDEKIAH
ACCESSION
How Jehoram came to power
Kings dates his start to the fifth year of Joram of Israel, "Jehoshaphat being then king of Judah". 2 Kings 8:16
Chronicles says that once he was established he killed all his brothers and some of Israel's princes. 2 Chronicles 21:4
SUCCESSION
The two kingdoms
THE VERDICT
How Scripture judges the reign
“and he did evil in the sight of the LORD”
2 Kings 8:18 (KJV) →
“And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife”
2 Kings 8:18 (KJV) →
BUT ALSO
Yet the LORD would not destroy Judah "for David his servant's sake", having promised him a light. 2 Kings 8:19 2 Chronicles 21:7
Chronicles adds that he "departed without being desired". 2 Chronicles 21:20
CHRONICLES GIVES IT AS
“and he wrought that which was evil in the eyes of the LORD”
2 Chronicles 21:6 (KJV) →
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS
✓ Did right ✕ Did evil ◐ Mixed ● No verdict formula
THE KINGDOM
Jerusalem and the places of the reign
Judah (the south) · tribe of Judah. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE NATION
What the nation did
He walked "in the way of the kings of Israel" like the house of Ahab. 2 Kings 8:18
He made high places in the mountains of Judah (Chronicles). 2 Chronicles 21:11
PROPHETS
Prophets of the reign
El Elijah “And thou shalt have great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day.”
ON THE WORLD STAGE
The powers of the day
ISRAEL (THE HOUSE OF OMRI)
Jehoram (Joram) son of Ahab · Ahab
TWO ACCOUNTS
Where Kings and Chronicles differ
Each ribbon joins the two accounts of one matter, passage to passage.
His end
2 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
His sons
2 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
Only in Chronicles
2 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
8 years (2 Kgs 8:17). Scripture gives lengths and cross-dates, never BC years.
THIELE, REVISED BY MCFALL (1991)
Shared rule with Jehoshaphat, 854–848 BC
Printed form: 848–841; co-regency from 854 (PDF p. 18).
YOUNG (2005), REVISING THIELE
Shared rule with Jehoshaphat, 854–848 BC
Printed form: 848–841; co-regency from 854/853 (p. 246 (Table 2)).
ALBRIGHT (1945)
Printed form: c. 849–842 (p. 21).
TRADITIONAL DATES (USSHER, 1658)
Shared rule with Jehoshaphat, 898–889 BC
Printed form: 889–885; co-regency from 898 (viceroy, A.M. 3106) / 892 (consort, A.M. 3112) (p. 48 (scan leaf n29)).
A viceroy and then a consort before reigning alone
James Ussher (1658)
Ussher made Jehoram viceroy in 898 BC and his father's consort in 892, reigning alone from 889. 2 Kings 1:17 2 Kings 8:16 [106]
A co-regency with Jehoshaphat from 854 BC
L. McFall (1991), revising E. R. Thiele

2 Kgs 1:17 counts from Jehoram's co-regency (from September 854); 2 Kgs 8:16 marks his sole reign from 848; the phrase "Jehoshaphat being then king" need not be cut from the text. 2 Kings 1:17 2 Kings 3:1 2 Kings 8:16 [117]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 4
1 Kings 22 2 Kings 1 2 Kings 8 2 Chronicles 21
PASSAGES · 4
1 Kings 22:50 2 Kings 1:17 2 Kings 8:16–24 2 Chronicles 21:1–20
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not name Jehoram's mother. He is one of only two kings of Judah whose mother Kings leaves out; the other is Ahaz.
Kings does not name Jehoram's wife at this point; it calls her "the daughter of Ahab". Her name, Athaliah, comes with her son's record.
Scripture does not say when Elijah wrote the letter.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the textHe is called both Jehoram and Joram in the same chapter of Kings. He is not the Jehoram (Joram) son of Ahab who reigned in Israel at the same time. 2 Kings 8:16 2 Kings 8:21 2 Kings 8:25
